title: Cardinality is monotone under decided inclusion
statement: If the decided inclusion subsetB s t evaluates to true then the size of s is at most the size of t.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.card_le_of_subsetB : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x2 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.subsetB x0 x1) Bool.true) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.Finset.card x0) (AxNat.Finset.card x1))))

evidence.supports: Nat.Finset.card_le_of_subsetB is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.Finset.card_le_of_subsetB 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x2 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.subsetB x0 x1) Bool.true) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.Finset.card x0) (AxNat.Finset.card x1))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is a DISTINGUISHING substring of the admitted type, not the theorem's name: an existence check would still pass if the statement drifted. Verified to fail on a perturbed pattern before this row was written. `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check.

evidence.supports: The definitions this statement is about COMPUTE the intended values, with negative controls -- the kernel cannot tell a Definition is wrong
evidence.notes: `Nat.Finset`'s operations are admitted on their TYPE; a `card` that computed the wrong number would have the right type, an empty axiom footprint, and would pass every other check in this ledger. `finset_tests.rs` reduces each operation to a numeral or a Bool at tiny discriminating arguments and pairs every positive with the specific wrong formula its negative control rules out. It caught one wrong hand-computed expectation while being written.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by `nat_prelude/finset.rs` (lane finset-role, ADR-1577).

notes: `subsetB` ranges only over [0, bound s) while F:nat-countrange-le-of-subset wants Nat.Subset over the common bound bound s + bound t. The gap needs no second search: at an index at or above bound s, `memB s i = false`, so the Subset premise `memB s i = true` is refuted and the obligation is vacuous there. That is available only because `memB` truncates in its own definition. ADR-1577.
